tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

scope-prior-state-and-contribution: Section 1, p.3: the authors state what GPU4PySCF contained when they started and what their contributions add. Their own scope statement.
scope-density-fitting-small-medium: Section 1, p.3 and Section 2.1, p.4: the density fitting code targets small to medium molecules (under 200 atoms); larger molecules go to the existing direct SCF, which the paper does not cover.
scope-benchmark-dataset: Section 2.1, p.4 and Appendix A, Table 5, p.27: 13 molecules, 20-168 atoms, 8 elements, as the paper states. The two medium molecules are among the 13 (Table 5 lists 13 names).
setup-dft-protocol-a100: Section 2.1, p.4 and Figure 1 caption, p.5: def2-TZVPP, B3LYP, (99,590) grids, A100-80G, def2-universal-JKFIT. The paper's own timing setup.
setup-closed-shell-density-fitting: Section 2.2, p.5: all benchmark computations in that section are closed-shell with density fitting; three modules SCF, gradient, Hessian. Stated scope.
memory-hybrid-strategy: Section 2.1, p.4: the CPU-GPU hybrid storage strategy is the authors' own implementation, described as used in this work.
speedup-hessian-qchem-finite-difference: Section 2.2, p.5: the Q-Chem reference Hessians are finite difference because of a Q-Chem memory issue; the 2-3 factor is the authors' stated expectation, and the value says so as an expectation.
speedup-benchmark-scope-qchem-only: Section 2.2, p.4-5: only Q-Chem is benchmarked, Hessian only for 20-84 atoms, and settings cannot be fully aligned. Limits the paper states about its own benchmark.
cost-aws-instances: Figure 2 caption, p.6: the AWS prices and instance specs the cost estimate uses.
gradient-pure-dft-future-work: Section 2.2, p.5-6: the pure DFT gradient could be faster with a more efficient algorithm; left as future work. The J matrix engine is the paper's reference [23] (White and Head-Gordon, 'A J matrix engine'), so the parenthesis is supported.
pcm-reference-caveat-two-factors: Section 2.3, p.6: Q-Chem 6.1 has no density fitting SCF with PCM, so the speedups mix two factors; the algorithms differ. A caveat the authors state.
pcm-solvent-models-available: Section 2.3, p.6 and Section 3.3, p.14: four PCM variants available, SMD CDS cost almost negligible, generalized Born not implemented.
pcm-implementation-details: Section 3.3, p.14: SWIG smoothing, NWChem Fortran and Python Lebedev re-implementation of SASA/CDS, SMD18 radii. The authors' own implementation description.
solvent-pcm-gpu-reengineered: Section 4.2, p.24: PCM/SMD re-engineered for GPU in Python, possible memory optimization needed, in PySCF v2.4 and Hessian in v2.6.
li-solvation-setup: Section 3.1.3, p.9: basis, auxiliary basis, IEF-PCM with UFF radii and dielectric 20.0, M06-2X-D3 zero damping, MD of 2.25M LiFSI in DMC:EC 51:49. The paper says the example is illustrative only.
chelpg-setup: Section 3.2.1, p.11: grid spacing 0.3, radial extent 2.8, Bondi radii with H at 1.1, B3LYP/def2-SVPD with density fitting.
nmr-giao-implementation: Section 3.2.2, p.13-14 and Figure 8 caption: GIAO implementation, toluene example with B3LYP/def2-TZVPP/def2-universal-JKFIT.
smd-solvation-dataset-and-uncertainty: Section 3.3, p.15 and Table 3 caption: dataset sizes for PySCF and G03, reference uncertainties, and the note that the database moved to version 2020 after SMD. The paper's stated benchmark basis.
mobh35-setup-and-limits: Section 3.4.1, p.15-16: subset covers three transition-metal rows, geomeTRIC used, the authors could not verify modified transition states, and no automated reaction-profile approach is provided. Setup plus limits the authors state.
api-to-gpu-to-cpu: Section 4.1, p.22: from v1.0 the patching is dropped and to_gpu/to_cpu convert objects; Listing 1 shows the water example. The paper's own API design.
func-ecp-cpu-only: Section 4.2, p.24: ECP is computed once on CPU via PySCF; acceptable for few heavy atoms; GPU ECP is future work.
func-dispersion-nonlocal: Section 4.2, p.23-24: dispersion corrections use dftd3/dftd4 without GPU (OpenMP disabled in the rebuild); nonlocal corrections optimized at CUDA level.
func-libraries-cuda: Section 4.3, p.25: CuPy, cuTENSOR default contraction engine, customized API for experimental CUDA LibXC (v6.2).
func-wavefunction-preliminary: Section 5, p.25: only preliminary MP2 and CCSD implementations. Table 4 (Hessian rows FD or CPU for several features) agrees with the second clause; the Table 4 text layer is partly garbled but the legend defines FD and CPU.
limits-general-not-optimal: Section 5, p.25-26: implementations 'certainly not optimal', many limitations; the section lists wavefunction methods, direct SCF integral schemes, PBC, multi-GPU and mixed precision as future work.
limits-low-level-api-incompatible: Section 5, p.26: low-level APIs of PySCF and GPU4PySCF are not fully compatible, so packages using low-level PySCF APIs cannot be directly accelerated.
limits-pbc-not-ported: Section 5, p.25-26: CPU PBC screening techniques may not transfer directly to GPU; new techniques are under development (ref [111]).
setup-learn-unitary-from-tn-states: Introduction, p.2: 'Our setup is to learn a target unitary operator through data samples encoded into TN states'; the setup is also defined in the Tensor network machine learning section.
def-predicting-risk: Eq. (1), p.2: the predicting risk is defined as a Haar integral of a trace-norm distance between projectors; the paper calls it the prediction error. The text layer garbles the formula but the surrounding words match the value.
def-unitary-embedded-mps-and-loss: p.2: unitary embedded MPS (D x D x d tensor to Dd x Dd unitary), labeled training set S, and the squared-norm loss are all defined in the main text.
theorem1-proof-route: p.3 and SI.B: the authors state the approximations their proof rests on (approximate unitary 2-design, mapping to a 1D Ising partition function, averaging over M and S). This is a statement of the proof's assumptions, not of a result.
mps-nfl-learned-unitary-form: p.3 and SI.B (near Eq. S33): the authors state the simplifying assumption M-dagger P_S = e^{i theta} I_tk (+) Y with Y in an (n-k)-qudit subsystem 'for simplicity'. The value matches.
mpo-one-moment-integral-trace-y: SI.A, Eqs. (S10)-(S12): the paper proves the integral of tr[Y]tr[Y*] equals 1 for a random unitary-embedded periodic MPO, by a loop-counting argument with the 1-moment Haar integral (S11); each loop gives a 1/(D'd') factor that cancels. The proof is diagrammatic but complete, and the result does not depend on D' or d'.
mps-nfl-proof-inequalities: SI.B, near (S33) and (S46): the authors state they use tr[AB] <= tr[A]tr[B] for PSD matrices and the Cauchy-Schwarz-type trace inequality for PSD F with tr(F)=1. This is a statement of proof steps that make the result a lower bound. Both inequalities are standard and correctly used.
def-directed-polyomino: SI.II.B, Definition 1: a directed polyomino as a finite subset of Z x Z rooted at (x0,y0), with the right/up closure condition. The value matches.
peps-trained-zone-assumption: SI.II.D (the step before the Eq. S34-like decomposition, Fig. S3): 'we consider the case that a subspace comprising k sites on lattice can be fully trained'. A stated simplifying assumption of the proof.
limitation-noise-finite-measurements-unt: Discussion, p.4: the authors name noise, finite measurement times and experimental validation on real quantum hardware as future work, so the analysis does not cover them.
scope-linearly-independent-training-set: p.2 ('for simplicity, we suppose that the states in the training set are linearly independent') and SI.I: 'we suppose that all of the MPOs or MPSs appeared in this work are unitary embedded'. Stated assumptions that limit the theorems.
data-acquisition-scale: Section 1, p.4: all data taken on Aquila on June 9, 2023, 96,250 measurements over 1,884 tasks. The paper's own data description.
rb87-room-temperature-device: Section 1.2, p.5: the paper's description of its hardware (Rb-87 atoms cooled by lasers in a vacuum cell). Vendor white paper, stated as the device setup, not a performance claim.
four-key-ingredients: Section 1.2, p.5-6: the four ingredients the authors say Aquila relies on. Architecture description by the vendor.
two-qubit-types-analog-only: Section 1.2, p.7: Aquila currently uses only the ground-Rydberg qubit in analog mode. The lifetime and interaction remarks about the two qubit types are general descriptions in the same sentence; the scope fact is what the paper settles.
readout-by-atom-presence: Section 1.2, p.7: Rydberg readout by re-trapping and fluorescence; absence means Rydberg, presence means ground. The paper's own readout description.
destructive-measurement-slow-shots: Section 1.2, p.7 and the full-cycle text, p.13: measurements are destructive, the array is rebuilt every shot, and the shot rate is under 10 Hz today.
site-geometry-limits: Section 1.2, p.9: 4 micrometer minimum site spacing and the 75 x 76 micrometer area, with premium access relaxing them. Hardware limits stated by the vendor (units garbled in the text layer but the quotes show them).
row-constraint: Section 1.2, p.9: sites must lie in rows at least 4 micrometers apart; a design decision to speed sorting, not fundamental, relaxable in premium mode.
two-photon-rydberg-drive: Section 1.2, p.11: the ground-Rydberg drive is a two-photon transition at 420 and 1013 nm via an off-resonant intermediate state.
detuning-definition-and-phase: Section 1.2 derivation box, p.10: detuning is defined as the off-resonance of the laser from the transition; the phase can be set to zero at the start by U(1) symmetry.
rotating-wave-approximation-used: Section 1.2 derivation box, p.10: the paper's rotating-frame derivation neglects the fast term by the rotating wave approximation. The value states only what the paper does; it is a textbook step, not a theorem, and the paper notes it is done for a time-independent two-state case.
analog-mode-definition: Section 1.2, p.11: analog mode is defined as specifying time series of Rabi rate, detuning, phase and atom positions, with interactions always on.
analog-mode-not-universal: Section 1.2, p.11: the authors state analog-mode computation is not necessarily universal and is specialized for some tasks.
rydberg-hamiltonian-control-parameters: Section 1.3, p.14: the Rydberg Hamiltonian and its four control parameters are defined by the paper.
measurements-in-z-basis-only: Section 1.3, p.14: measurements are restricted to the logical Z basis only.
van-der-waals-sixth-power: Section 1.3 Hamiltonian and Sections 1.2 and 3, p.12 and p.23: the interaction term is defined as C6/|r|^6 between Rydberg-state atoms. A defined model term of the paper, not a measured result.
interaction-strength-examples: Section 1.2, p.12 and Section 3, p.23: worked values of the defined law. Checked: C6 = 5,420,503 gives about 20.7 at 8 um, 1,323 at 4 um and 0.32 at 16 um, matching the stated 20, 1,320 and 0.32. Units are partly lost in the text layer.
rydberg-blockade-definition: Section 1.2, p.12, the sentence 'This is the origin of the so-called Rydberg Blockade: within a certain radius, called the blockade radius, the low-energy subspace ... excludes the doubly excited Rydberg state'. Defines the blockade and the blockade radius for the paper.
static-and-dynamic-blockade-radius: Section 3, p.23: static and dynamic blockade radii are defined with their conditions (positive detuning and zero Rabi drive; zero detuning and nonzero Rabi drive) and the paper notes either may be meant.
rabi-enhancement-setup-n7: Section 3.2, p.24-25 and Figure 3.2 caption: distances, Rabi frequencies (15 for N up to 4, 5.0 for N=7) and the stated loss of scale separation for larger N. The paper's own setup.
error-source-laser-noise: Section 1.4, p.15: the authors state laser phase and amplitude noise as an error source of their device.
error-source-atom-motion: Section 1.4, p.15: the authors state thermal motion as an error source (Doppler detuning variance, position-dependent interaction).
error-source-decoherence-scattering: Section 1.4, p.15: incoherent decay via the intermediate and Rydberg states is stated as a major error source, with loss possible with the drive off.
error-source-inhomogeneity-measurement: Section 1.4, p.15: imperfect holography gives array inhomogeneity, and state measurement (loss or imperfect anti-trapping) is a leading error source.
datasheet-conservative-limits: Section 1.5, p.16: the restrictions were set within Aquila's limits and can be relaxed; certain experiments in the paper go beyond them (10 us, 115 um). Units garbled in the text layer.
datasheet-metric-definitions: Section 1.5 datasheet, p.17: definitions of the Ramsey and spin-echo dephasing times and of the false-negative and false-positive detection errors, as stated in the datasheet table.
braket-evolution-time-restriction: Figure 2.2 caption, p.19: the maximum time exceeds the 4 us Braket restriction and is available in premium access mode.
short-times-restriction-wording: Section 2.1, p.19: short times under 100 ns are limited by finite laser rise and fall time, which restricts valid programs.
lp-analogue-not-a-gate: Section 3.3, p.26: the return probabilities are not gate fidelities, and no gate is executed because Aquila lacks the hyperfine states.
z2-chain-exceeds-braket-range: Figure 4.2 caption, p.31: the maximum time and Y extent (115.9 um greater than 76 um) may exceed the Braket range and need premium access.
2d-phases-setup: Section 4.3, p.31-32: 11 x 11 grid, adiabatic ramp from negative detuning, lattice spacings 5.9 and 7.0 um, as the paper states.
scar-exceeds-braket-time: Figure 5.2 caption, p.34: the maximum time exceeds the 4 us Braket restriction and is available in premium access mode.
mis-instance-setup: Section 6, p.35-36 and Figure 6.1: King's graph with 30% dropout, 16 x 16 with 183 vertices and MIS 60, spacing 5 um, final detuning optimized by a 1D grid search on one instance.
mis-post-processing-and-definition: Section 6, p.36: mIS defined as a non-extendable independent set that may not be maximum, plus the two-step greedy post-processing, as the paper describes.
framework-definition: Abstract, p.1 and Section 1: the framework the paper introduces (system-only layers combined with trainable ancilla-assisted dissipative modules).
dissipative-block-stinespring-channel: Section 3.2, Eq. (8), p.4: the dissipative block is defined as a parameterized Stinespring dilation with ancillas in zero, a joint unitary and trace-out, so it is a CPTP map on the system.
dissipative-block-implementation-iswap: Section 3.2, p.4 and Appendix A.1, p.13-14: single-qubit rotations plus fully connected system-ancilla iSWAP, nm iSWAPs per round. The paper's own circuit.
dissipative-vqe-protocol: Section 3.3, Eqs. (9)-(11), p.4-5: the recursive protocol, ancilla reset each round, and the final-energy loss are defined by the paper.
dissipative-recovery-protocol: Section 3.4, Eqs. (12)-(17), p.5: same block without system-only layers, fidelity metric F_T = Tr(rho_T rho_tar) for a pure target, loss 1 - F_T.
benchmark-hamiltonian-and-reference: Section 4.1, Eq. (18), p.6: the nearest-neighbor spin Hamiltonian with XX/YY/ZZ couplings and local fields, with exact diagonalization references.
recovery-target-states: Section 4.1, Eqs. (19)-(21), p.6: W state, uniform superposition and dressed cluster state with D=3 and angles pi/4.
recovery-default-simulation-settings: Figure 5 caption, p.8: defaults n=3, m=3, lr=0.8, T=3, p=0.1 unless stated otherwise.
appendix-original-vqa-definition: Appendix B.1, Definition 1, Eqs. (25)-(26), p.15: original VQA defined as a product of parameterized gates with cost Tr[O rho].
appendix-dissipative-vqa-definition: Appendix B.1, Definition 2, Eqs. (27)-(30), p.15: reset-assisted non-unital channel with reset probability q, mainly q=1.
appendix-gd-and-gap-definitions: Appendix B.2, Eqs. (31)-(32), p.15-16: gradient descent update, one-step decrease and optimality gap are defined.
assumption1-smoothness: Appendix B.2, Assumption 1, p.16: stated assumption of the analysis (beta-smoothness, step size at most 1/beta, beta poly(n)). It limits Theorems 1 and 2; the paper does not show it holds for the dissipative cost beyond the remark about local Hamiltonians.
assumption2-two-design: Appendix B.2, Assumption 2, p.16: stated assumption of 2-design initialization with zero mean gradient. Stated as an assumption, not shown.
assumption3-pl-dissipative: Appendix B.2, Assumption 3, Eq. (34), p.16: a Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition assumed for the dissipative cost. The paper assumes it and never verifies it; the value says 'posits'.
assumption4-trajectory-flatness: Appendix B.2, Assumption 4, Eq. (35), p.16: a trajectory-uniform flatness assumption for the original VQA, assumed and not verified.
lemma1-descent-lower-bound: Appendix B.3, Lemma 1, p.16: statement with conditions (beta-smooth, 0<eta<=1/beta) and a complete proof via the quadratic upper bound (S37) and eta(1 - beta eta/2) >= eta/2. The conclusion inequality (S36) appears in the text layer. Checked, correct.
lemma2-descent-upper-bound: Appendix B.3, Lemma 2, p.16-17: statement with conditions (Hessian norm <= beta on the segment, 0<eta<=1/beta) and a complete Taylor-based proof giving the 3 eta/2 bound (S39)-(S40). Checked, correct.
lemma3-pl-contraction: Appendix B.3, Lemma 3, p.17: statement with conditions (beta-smooth, PL, 0<eta<=1/beta) and a proof from Lemma 1 and the PL inequality giving (1 - eta mu) <= e^{-eta mu}. Checked, correct.
lemma4-flat-vqa-step-lower-bound: Appendix B.3, Lemma 4, p.17: statement with its conditions (Assumptions 1 and 4, expected gap above delta0 and then below eps) and a proof that sums Lemma 2's per-step bound over T steps. The result is conditional on Assumption 4, which the paper assumes, and the value says so.
theorem1-dissipative-polynomial-converge: Appendix B.3, Theorem 1, p.17-18: stated under Assumptions 1 and 3 and proved by applying Lemma 3 with eta = 1/beta and solving for T. The result holds only under the assumed PL condition, which the value states.
theorem2-conditional-exponential-separat: Appendix B.3, Theorem 2, p.18: stated with its conditions (Theorem 1 assumptions, eta m <= poly(n), Assumption 4, E[Delta0] >= delta0) and proved by combining Theorem 1 and Lemma 4. The paper calls the advantage conditional, as the value does; the PL and flatness hypotheses are unverified assumptions.
theory-limit-no-unconditional-convergenc: Appendix B.3, closing remark, p.18: the authors state that global convergence is not proven from the cited barren-plateau paper alone and holds only under a global PL condition and trajectory-uniform flatness.
open-problem-scaling-and-resources: Section 5, p.10: the authors state that scaling with system size, resource dependence on task and error model, and use in other variational algorithms are still to be understood.

theory_low.theorem1-mps-nfl-conditions: Theorem 1 (p.3) has only a sketch in the main text; the full proof is SI.B. The SI proof replaces the risk by a norm-concentration approximation, treats the U(k) as an approximate unitary 2-design, assumes the learned unitary has the block form with Y acting on an (n-k)-qudit subsystem 'for simplicity', and uses inequalities and approximation signs. Those assumptions are not in the theorem statement or the quotes. Also the closed-form Eq. (2) is garbled in the text layer. Not a clean proved result as quoted.
theory_low.mps-nfl-risk-monotone-and-limits: Monotonic decrease is a numerical observation (Fig. 2 and S4, n=4 and 5 only). The endpoint claims come from SI.B Eqs. (S31)-(S32), (S47)-(S48), which use approximation signs ('approximates to 1' and 'approximates to 0'), not exact bounds. A measured result plus an approximate derivation.
theory_low.mps-nfl-average-depends-on-size-only: An authors' reading of Eq. (2). The bound also depends on D and d (A and B), as the paper itself says on p.4. 'Solely' means only the training-set size among the data-dependent quantities. Interpretation, not a result.
theory_low.mpo-from-states-nfl-bound: SI.A: the orthonormal case (S9)-(S14) is derived with a lower-bound sign and rests on norm concentration and an approximate 2-design. Cases (b) and (c) are covered by 'Similar calculations also apply', with no separate derivation, and (S15)-(S16) switch to equality without a stated reason. The value's equality claims are not proved in the paper.
theory_low.mps-empty-training-set-risk: SI.B, (S31)-(S32), (S47)-(S48): the paper writes 'approximates to 1' for the empty set and 'approximates to 0' for the full set, using approximation signs (and tk=n gives dn only approximately). Approximate results, not exact proved statements.
theory_low.theorem2-peps-nfl-conditions: Theorem 2 (p.3, SI.II): the bound contains an unspecified constant c and relies on Corollary 1, which is Theorem 1 of Ref. [68] and is only cited. The SI also says the higher-order terms are dropped in the thermodynamic limit (S94), and it uses the same norm-concentration and training-subspace simplifications as Theorem 1. Not proved in full here; and the formula is garbled in the text layer.
theory_low.theorem2-peps-bound-depends-on-size: p.3: the authors' reading of Theorem 2, which itself rests on the cited Corollary 1 of [68], an unspecified constant c, and a thermodynamic-limit approximation. Interpretation of a bound that is not fully proved here.
theory_low.peps-2moment-is-2d-ising-partition-funct: Introduction p.2 and proof sketch p.3: a method statement. The polyomino method and the bound on the partition function are taken from Ref. [68] (Theorem 3 and Corollary 1 in the SI are cited, 'details of proof ... in Ref. [68]').
theory_low.peps-norm-concentration: SI.II.A, Eq. (S52): the concentration bound rests on Corollary 1 (Theorem 1 of Ref. [68]) for the 2-moment bound 1 + c(0.7)^L, which is cited, not proved here; it also assumes 1-design and 2-design behavior of each local unitary. The variance expression uses an unspecified constant c.
theory_low.peps-proof-decomposition-z1-z5: SI.II.D: an intermediate step of the Theorem 2 proof (splitting Z into five terms, three bounded by the cited Corollary 1). A step in an argument that depends on a cited result, not a result in itself; equations garbled in the text layer.
theory_low.peps-nfl-thermodynamic-limit-and-edge-ca: SI.II.E, (S94)-(S96): the bound is obtained by ignoring higher-order terms in the L-to-infinity limit. The k=0 and k=L^2 cases are outside the range k in [1, L^2-1] that Theorem 2 states. Approximate, derived from a bound that rests on a cited result.
theory_low.nfl-tn-vs-classical-comparison: p.3-4: the classical formula is cited from the literature [73-75] and the comparison is the authors' interpretation of their bound.
theory_low.conclusion-intrinsic-limitations: Summary, p.4: the authors' interpretation of their bounds (which are not fully proved, see Theorems 1 and 2). A conclusion, not a settled result.
theory_low.blockade-insensitive-to-exact-interactio: Section 1.2, p.12: the authors' physical explanation (large doubly excited energy so it can be adiabatically eliminated). It is a model approximation argued in words, not defined or derived in the paper.
theory_low.rabi-enhancement-sqrt-n-derivation: Section 3.2, p.24: a one-line matrix-element argument in the strict blockade limit, not a stated and proved theorem. The paper's own N=7 data show non-blockaded dynamics, and the value states an idealized result as general. An idealized physics argument with its measured check, not a proved result.
theory_low.ordered-states-blockade-picture: Section 4, p.29: an intuitive picture stated without derivation or proof.
theory_low.z2-readout-probability-estimate: Section 4.1, p.30: a back-of-envelope estimate (0.92^6 about 60%) from an 8% measurement error that is itself a fitted or inferred value. An estimate, not a settled result.
theory_low.mis-mapping-blockade-radius: Section 6, p.36: a method statement; the encoding argument is attributed to [Ebadi2022] ('For more details, see [Ebadi2022]'), a cited result.
